solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stirring icy gin, he should get clean

indicators.note: stirring a drink mixes it up, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man mixing an icy gin is told he ought to be sober and clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' rearranges ICY GIN HE; 'should get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hygienic means sanitary and free of germs, which is a sense of clean.

clue.text: Cleo's new ideology reveals grammatical flaw

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the name are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the letters of Cleo plus the S of the possessive
an ism is a doctrine or ideology

explanation.surface: Cleopatra's latest political belief exposes a fault in her grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CLEOS into SOLEC; the S of 'Cleo's' counts here.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a mistake in grammar or usage, a grammatical error.

clue.text: Everyday fare served up in exotic plates by parliament

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and altered, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in Japan or historically Germany

explanation.surface: Ordinary meals are dished up on fancy plates beside the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges PLATES into STAPLE; 'served up in' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple diet is the basic food eaten regularly, ordinary daily fare.

clue.text: Bridge partners mentioned river siesta

parts.note: in the card game bridge, South and North play as partners

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the river's name is given by its sound

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Card-table partners talked about a river during an afternoon nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' turns OUSE, a river in Yorkshire and elsewhere in England, into its sound-alike OOZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooze is a short sleep, much like an afternoon siesta.

clue.text: Last word in steam engines

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: The final say on the subject of steam locomotives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters running across steAM ENgines.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is the word said at the close of a prayer, so it is literally a last word.

clue.text: Left one with Bert struggling to find the words

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: struggling suggests things in disarray, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Bert, left on his own, battles to come up with the right words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges BERT into BRET; 'with' and 'find' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera or musical, the words sung.

clue.text: Hundreds on planet in want

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, so several hundreds
Earth is a planet

explanation.surface: With hundreds of people on the planet living in poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, the noun sense of want.

clue.text: Time when cricketers might appear?

parts.note: a clock hour that is also the number in a cricket side, so the team could show up then

explanation.surface: Asking at what hour the cricket players are due to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket team is called by the number of its players.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket team has that number of players, and it is also an hour on the clock.

clue.text: Tony goes mad about company magnate

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters wrap the abbreviation
going mad means losing order, so the name's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Tony loses his temper over a business and its powerful boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes mad' looks like a description of Tony; it makes TYON, which 'about' wraps around the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy and powerful business magnate.

clue.text: Included hug before first of dates

indicators.note: before places the hug ahead of the following letter

parts.note: to hug is to embrace

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cuddle was part of things before the first romantic outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace something can mean to take it in or include it.

clue.text: Philip and Edward have to stop talking

parts.note: Pip is a short form of Philip
Ed is a short form of Edward
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Two men named Philip and Edward are told to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipe down is an informal idiom meaning be quiet or stop talking.

clue.text: Partly rewrites the record book

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A volume that revises the historical account in part.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is rewritES THE Record.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament in the Bible.

clue.text: Footballer from batting team got out

parts.note: in cricket the batting side is said to be in
a side is a team
left means went out or departed

explanation.surface: A football player emerges from the batting team who have just been dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside left was a forward position in older football formations, so a player.

clue.text: Course of salts

definitions.meaning: a famous racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby
a kind of bath salts, magnesium sulphate, named after a Surrey town

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the same Surrey town, south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey town gives its name to a racecourse and to medicinal salts.

clue.text: Appointing group of church workers during Advent

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival
a mission is a group sent out by a church

explanation.surface: Choosing church staff in the weeks before Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advent' looks like the season but means arrival here.
explanation.definitionFit: Commissioning means formally appointing someone to a post or task.

clue.text: Popular without little bit of money? That's naive

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
no means having none, without
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Someone popular but penniless is called gullible.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent can mean guileless or artless, a sense of naive.

clue.text: At that place drinks initially will be on the rocks

parts.note: in there means at that place

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Drinks over there will be served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' suggests a drink with ice; here it means financially troubled. 'will be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in debt or loss-making is like being in financial trouble, close to ruin.

clue.text: Produce infusion of green tea

indicators.note: an infusion steeps and mixes leaves, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Make a brew of green tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate is to produce or create something.

clue.text: Penny put on weight in spring

indicators.note: put on places the first piece on top of the second in this down clue

parts.note: an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Penny gained weight during the springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to spring suddenly upon something.

clue.text: Prohibit an Australian fruit

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit

explanation.surface: Banning a fruit from Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Proposing sex not allowed round home

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the outer phrase wraps the inner one

parts.note: no mating means sex is forbidden
in means at home

explanation.surface: Suggesting a ban on sex in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominating someone is putting them forward, proposing them.

clue.text: Caught — but scored?

definitions.meaning: trapped in a net, as fish are
in football, putting the ball into the goal's net

explanation.surface: Asking whether a captured fish counts as a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Netting a catch or a goal both use the net, giving caught and scored.

clue.text: It's a tricky problem if this vegetable is hot

definitions.text: It's a tricky problem if this vegetable is hot

parts.words: It's a tricky problem if this vegetable is hot
parts.note: points to the idiom for a controversial issue nobody wants to handle, named after a root vegetable

explanation.surface: A thorny issue arises when a certain vegetable is too hot to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot one of these tubers is an idiom for a controversial issue.

clue.text: Seat in church not finished

indicators.note: not finished means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a cathedral is a major church

explanation.surface: A pew in a church still under construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' removes the last letter, L; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathedra is the bishop's throne, a seat of authority in Latin.

clue.text: Shy actors

definitions.meaning: to throw, as in a coconut shy

explanation.surface: Performers who are bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as timid but is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast is to throw, and the cast are a play's actors.

clue.text: American misbehaves behind closed doors

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A US citizen behaves badly in private.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal phrase meaning in private, not in open court.

clue.text: Dismiss article — this issue's volcanic

parts.note: to eject is to throw out or dismiss
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Throwing out a newspaper piece because this edition is explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a magazine edition but means matter thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejecta are material thrown out by a volcano, so a volcanic discharge.

clue.text: After preparing tea, TV's dead — heartbroken!

indicators.note: preparing a drink involves mixing, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters TV plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Having made a cuppa, someone finds the television broken and is distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After preparing' reads as making a cuppa but is the anagram signal; the S of 'TV's' counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Devastated means overwhelmed with grief or shock, heartbroken.
